source.title: Instance-Dependent Generalization Bounds via Optimal Transport
source.authors: Song-Yan Hou; Parnian Kassraie; Anastasis Kratsios; A. Krause; Jonas Rothfuss

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proposes and evaluates instance-dependent generalization bounds. Its experiments report bound values and how those values respond to regularization, network size, and partitioning; they do not test the claim versions’ specified training-error/test-error outcomes or measures.
record.gate_note: The empirical results concern calculated upper bounds on risk or the generalization gap, not measured train/test gaps. The paper’s statements about actual generalization effects of adversarial training, weight decay, early stopping, and over-parameterization are descriptions of prior work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study derives and evaluates bounds using local Lipschitz regularity in input space. Its own experiments measure bound values, not the held-out performance comparisons in V1–V6 or V8, or the magnitude-scaled weight sharpness and gap rankings in V7. Width-dependent bound values do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their localized, instance-dependent bounds remain relatively tight for over-parameterized models and reflect selected regularization effects. They suggest local regularity matters for generalization and distributional robustness. These conclusions concern theoretical guarantees and calculated bounds, rather than direct tests of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives and evaluates optimal-transport generalization bounds, rather than testing the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The calculated bounds vary with partition size; the authors report that they initially decrease and then increase as partitioning becomes finer. The bound also changes with training sample size and with regularization settings in figure-only sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected partition-based classification bound decreases from 1.447 to 0.478 as sample size increases from 2560 to 81920 and is substantially smaller than the global and uniform comparison bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Localized instance-dependent bounds can provide tighter classification-risk guarantees than the compared global and uniform bounds on this synthetic task.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports improved calculated bounds with adversarial training, weight decay, and early stopping; Figure 2 reports only minor bound changes over a roughly thousandfold parameter-count increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed bound responds to selected training regularizers and remains comparatively insensitive to network size in the synthetic regression and classification experiments.

record.problems: The empirical results assess calculated bounds rather than actual held-out error gaps. The experiments use synthetic 1D regression and 2D binary classification tasks with fully connected networks. Regularization and network-size trends are presented in figures, without extracted numerical values here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Figures 1 and 2 report bound trends without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text; the cited comparison values in Table 1 are not separate interventions on the claim’s specified behavior.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus fixed random-label fitting and held-out accuracy.
Training interpolation and continued reductions in measured test error as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning, including recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with measured generalization gaps, and comparative rankings against norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix D.2 specifies leaky-ReLU networks trained with AdamW, with weight decay zero by default, despite the main text's generic SGD description. The reported uncertainties are standard errors over 10 seeds. The Table 1 entries are selected bound minima and should be retained only as bound-method results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label and random-label training or report their train/test accuracies.
Does not measure test error across widths around the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image datasets.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or measure its effect on held-out performance.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other gap measures.
Does not remove or compare memorized training examples.
